item.title: Shelton Eyes End to US Men’s Grand Slam Drought
item.description: [Bloomberg] Ben Shelton heads into the US Open final with a chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, potentially giving US men’s tennis a new marquee star. Bloomberg News Business of Sports Reporter Vanessa Perdomo joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss Shelton and also broader questions across sports ranging from college eligibility rules to the NFL’s push into international markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Will Silicon Valley Rearm America?
item.description: [Bloomberg] War in Ukraine, conflict in the Middle East and the rise of China have pushed national security back to the center of US economic and industrial strategy. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper says the country needs to spend more on defense and better use cutting-edge weapons coming out of places like Silicon Valley, Austin and Boston. The opportunity is particularly striking in space, where companies like Apex Space are trying to industrialize satellite production as the US considers ambitious projects like Golden Dome . But the new defense-tech boom still faces hard questions: will the Pentagon procure quickly enough; will startups scale production; is space-based missile defense technically and financially realistic; and will the future belong to startups, legacy primes, or a marriage between the two? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LIV Golf’s $5 Billion Path to Bankruptcy
item.description: [Bloomberg] LIV shook professional golf with flashy tournaments and big payouts, thanks to billions of dollars in backing from the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. On today’s Big Take podcast, David Gura and Golf.com senior writer Sean Zak look at why LIV Golf couldn’t make the cut — and how it changed pro golf. Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
